lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with: **Do you have a child or children that you're responsible for?** If yes, could you tell me how many children you have and their ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do have a child I'm responsible for. I have one child - Alex, who is 9 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have one child, Alex, who is 9 years old.

Now I need to ask: **Are you responsible for Alex?** This means do you live with Alex and are you the person who is primarily responsible for their care (such as providing for their daily needs, food, clothing, etc.)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. Alex lives with me and I'm the one who takes care of him - you know, all the day-to-day stuff like meals, clothes, getting him to school, all of that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you for confirming that.

Next question: **Where do you and Alex live?** Specifically, do you both live in the UK, or do either of you live elsewhere (such as Northern Ireland, or outside the UK)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: We both live in the UK - we're in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. 

Now I need to ask: **Are you or Alex subject to immigration control?** This means, do either of you have any restrictions on your stay in the UK, such as a visa condition that states you have "no recourse to public funds"?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, we don't have any restrictions like that. We're not subject to immigration control.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

One more important question: **Is there anyone else who is also claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or could someone else claim for him?** For example, does Alex live with another parent or guardian who might be claiming, or does he spend equal time between two households?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, there's no one else claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me - he lives with me full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! Based on the information you've provided, you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why you qualify:
- Alex is 9 years old (under the age limit of 16)
- You are responsible for Alex - he lives with you and you provide for his daily care
- You both live in the UK (Manchester)
- Neither of you have immigration restrictions
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

You can now proceed to make your Child Benefit claim. You can do this online through the government's official service or by post. You'll need Alex's birth certificate (or adoption certificate if applicable) when you apply.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
